convoLines.text: "Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Nina. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"The pantry's nearly bare. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at the creek bend, past the treeline and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"You're wrong." Too fast. Jesse looks away. "Just... drop it, okay?"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
They hear you out, but something in them stays guarded.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
"Still on that foraging help."
"Right. Go on, then."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"My theory changes weekly. This week's: we're the control group. Somewhere there's a village that got instructions, and we're the ones they just... watched. Cheerful thought, right?"
"Still on what you think happened to us."
"You want me to follow you into the dark? Earn that first."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Murkcap? Gianna is pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I've been writing letters I'll never send. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Nina. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"Thank you for hearing it. I needed someone to know — and I needed it to stop with you."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about that foraging help — we got cut off, 4 days back. 'Right. I get it. A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.'"
"It's already handled. Thank you for asking."
"Like I said — we're still on that foraging help."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
*You've watched them deflect before — the same smooth sidestep. Thin evidence won't hold them. Gather one more thread first.*
"Wow." Jesse looks hurt, then angry. "I share my food with you and this is what I get?"
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
You said you'd earn it, not that I should just hand it over. Fair. I'm watching — and so far, so good.
"There's still the matter of the murder of Nair. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about that foraging help — we got cut off, 7 days back. 'Wow. Jesse looks hurt, then angry. I share my food with you and this is what I get?'"
"It's already handled. Thank you for asking."
"that foraging help — that's still where we are."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
*They deflected you last time, and what you have hasn't grown since. One more thread before you speak, or they'll slip away again.*
"Nope. No." Jesse shakes their head too fast. "I don't know where you're getting this."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
The moment passes without landing. Not yet.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
DeShawn: "I've heard good things about Thornfield. We should link with them — we'd be stronger together."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"All right — let's ask them." You carry the proposal to Thornfield.
At the trap line the ground is torn up. Something was here, recently, and it wasn't careful. DeShawn's hand finds your sleeve. You leave together, faster than you came.
"Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
"Right, so — I believe in breakfast. In people showing up. Small, provable things. The big beliefs all broke — the small ones held."
"Still on what you believe in."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"They took Nino — Duel, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Meet me at the south slope below the meadow and we'll fill packs before dark."
As I said — Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"Oh." A long pause. "I didn't think it was anyone's. It's gone — I ate it days ago. I'm sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"As I said — we're still on that foraging help."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that foraging help."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«Non capisco niente. Niente di niente!» "Water?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Proprio così, parola mia.» They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
«Grazie. Davvero, grazie.» (you catch 'Grazie' — thanks) They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
«Non dimenticherò questo.» You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Tu sei... il capo?» (you catch 'capo' — boss)
Laura laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — È vero. Assolutamente vero." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
Nina: "Hey. I want to ask it plain: will you be my bonded friend? I'll watch your back if you watch mine."
"Stick together, then." They look steadier already.
"Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses. Ha."
"The way I read it — I count meals, not days. Three meals since the rain. Two since the alarm. Days are for people with calendars. I have a stomach."
"Funny thing — Still on what day it is."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"You know — I don't keep score on that. Score-keeping is how you stop sleeping. I do what the day needs and I don't rehearse it after."
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Good question." "They took you — Impress Us, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Ruth grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Ruth is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said you believe we get through this — the alternative doesn't work. Still holding the line?"
DeShawn has an edge today — something curdled.
"Giant Water Lily — crush the leaf, smell it, taste the stem. That's how you know it."
"This one — Amla. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them White Oak Acorns — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay, I'm all ears."
"Huh. Let me think about that." If we don't write it down, it didn't happen. I'm writing it all down.
"Every name, every day, every meal. The boring stuff is the important stuff."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Alright. Catch you later."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that personal stuff."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me your trade. I've been watching your hands since — they know things."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
They nod — and keep their distance, for now.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ruth nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Nino keeps their voice low. "The stores. Have you looked at the stores? We're running thin."
They nod. "Okay."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It keeps getting worse. I can't haul or hunt with it like this — and if it festers, I'm done for. Please, clean it out and bind it tight."
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"They'd tell me to keep working. So I'm working. That's the whole plan."
Ruth has an edge today — something curdled.
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Last time things were different. They always are." "We lost Yara and Chloe. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"People here talk. What they say about you when you're not at the fire — that's the real answer to your question."
"Still on each other."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Jesse nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.

lines: d9: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Olivia Keller is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d9: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d9: 🕯️ Olivia Keller is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d9: What Olivia kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d9: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Maya blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d9: 📖 LEARNED: Bodyguard (Level 1). In the wilds, when a blow is falling on someone beside you, you step into it. Once per fight, an attack meant for your ally lands on you instead. It hurts. That's the job.
d9: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.

d9: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d9: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d9: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Olivia Keller, 9 days. The mantle passes to Maya Moretti.
d9: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Maya Moretti, 32 — a crossing guard. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm.
d9: The fire knew Maya before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.
